## Detailed Description

Base class for objects that can produce a continuous stream of audio.

An [AudioSource](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1AudioSource.html "Base class for objects that can produce a continuous stream of audio.") has two states: 'prepared' and 'unprepared'.

When a source needs to be played, it is first put into a 'prepared' state by a call to [prepareToPlay()](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1AudioSource.html#a33632aded3deb6d35214cb86aed69d9e "Tells the source to prepare for playing."), and then repeated calls will be made to its [getNextAudioBlock()](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1AudioSource.html#afa18b8ebcf39f268b075c7833bb6b79d "Called repeatedly to fetch subsequent blocks of audio data.") method to process the audio data.

Once playback has finished, the [releaseResources()](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1AudioSource.html#a19b1b0a38d6666b94d8e86156d064768 "Allows the source to release anything it no longer needs after playback has stopped.") method is called to put the stream back into an 'unprepared' state.

See also[AudioFormatReaderSource](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1AudioFormatReaderSource.html "A type of AudioSource that will read from an AudioFormatReader."), [ResamplingAudioSource](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1ResamplingAudioSource.html "A type of AudioSource that takes an input source and changes its sample rate.")

## [◆](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1AudioSource.html\#a33632aded3deb6d35214cb86aed69d9e)prepareToPlay()

| virtual void juce::AudioSource::prepareToPlay | ( | int | _samplesPerBlockExpected_, |

Tells the source to prepare for playing.

An [AudioSource](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1AudioSource.html "Base class for objects that can produce a continuous stream of audio.") has two states: prepared and unprepared.

The [prepareToPlay()](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1AudioSource.html#a33632aded3deb6d35214cb86aed69d9e "Tells the source to prepare for playing.") method is guaranteed to be called at least once on an 'unprepared' source to put it into a 'prepared' state before any calls will be made to [getNextAudioBlock()](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1AudioSource.html#afa18b8ebcf39f268b075c7833bb6b79d "Called repeatedly to fetch subsequent blocks of audio data."). This callback allows the source to initialise any resources it might need when playing.

Once playback has finished, the [releaseResources()](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1AudioSource.html#a19b1b0a38d6666b94d8e86156d064768 "Allows the source to release anything it no longer needs after playback has stopped.") method is called to put the stream back into an 'unprepared' state.

Note that this method could be called more than once in succession without a matching call to [releaseResources()](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1AudioSource.html#a19b1b0a38d6666b94d8e86156d064768 "Allows the source to release anything it no longer needs after playback has stopped."), so make sure your code is robust and can handle that kind of situation.

Parameters

|     |     |
| --- | --- |
| samplesPerBlockExpected | the number of samples that the source will be expected to supply each time its [getNextAudioBlock()](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1AudioSource.html#afa18b8ebcf39f268b075c7833bb6b79d "Called repeatedly to fetch subsequent blocks of audio data.") method is called. This number may vary slightly, because it will be dependent on audio hardware callbacks, and these aren't guaranteed to always use a constant block size, so the source should be able to cope with small variations. |
| sampleRate | the sample rate that the output will be used at - this is needed by sources such as tone generators. |

See also[releaseResources](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1AudioSource.html#a19b1b0a38d6666b94d8e86156d064768 "Allows the source to release anything it no longer needs after playback has stopped."), [getNextAudioBlock](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1AudioSource.html#afa18b8ebcf39f268b075c7833bb6b79d "Called repeatedly to fetch subsequent blocks of audio data.")

Called repeatedly to fetch subsequent blocks of audio data.

After calling the [prepareToPlay()](https://docs.juce.com/master/classjuce_1_1AudioSource.html#a33632aded3deb6d35214cb86aed69d9e "Tells the source to prepare for playing.") method, this callback will be made each time the audio playback hardware (or whatever other destination the audio data is going to) needs another block of data.

It will generally be called on a high-priority system thread, or possibly even an interrupt, so be careful not to do too much work here, as that will cause audio glitches!

Tells the source to prepare for playing.

An AudioSource has two states: prepared and unprepared.

The prepareToPlay() method is guaranteed to be called at least once on an 'unprepared' source to put it into a 'prepared' state before any calls will be made to getNextAudioBlock(). This callback allows the source to initialise any resources it might need when playing.

Once playback has finished, the releaseResources() method is called to put the stream back into an 'unprepared' state.

Note that this method could be called more than once in succession without a matching call to releaseResources(), so make sure your code is robust and can handle that kind of situation.

This will be called when the source is no longer going to have its getNextAudioBlock() method called, so it should release any spare memory, etc. that it might have allocated during the prepareToPlay() call.
